name: Representative-position long-history ToMe engineering gate
status: engineering only; no efficacy inference authorized
question: At identical matching, memory trajectory rules, per-frame/window token quotas and total K/V budget, does retaining each ToMe destination token's SAM2 position embedding execute reliably compared with averaging position embeddings?

scope.targets: All post-prompt frames; the clip must include reads with more than six non-conditioning history maps.
scope.evidence_class: Real-clip engineering gate only. Frame scores are checked for pipeline and pre-compression parity, not used as efficacy evidence.
scope.cohort_status: PolypGen has informed prior development. This gate cannot support a confirmatory or generalization claim.

conditions.position_mean: Generic projected-key ToMe matching; fixed ten-map uniform history allocation; mass-weighted merge of memory and position embeddings; representative-position RoPE.
conditions.position_representative: Same configuration and matching; mass-weighted merge of memory content, but copy the ToMe destination's original SAM2 position embedding and use that same spatial coordinate for RoPE.

shared_design.sam2: Frozen SAM2.1 Hiera-Tiny; original image encoder, memory writes, frame schedule, dense queries, decoder, object scores and pointer path.
shared_design.history: Native conditioning map plus the same selected prior frame IDs, up to ten non-conditioning maps. No frame selection or confidence gates.
shared_design.budget: Keep one dense 4096-token conditioning map. With N<=6 prior maps retain all N*4096 tokens; for N>6 allocate exactly 24576 tokens over prior maps uniformly, remainder to newest ages. Pointers remain separate and uncompressed.
shared_design.matching: Pinned official ToMe bipartite soft matching on each layer's frozen SAM2 projected-key metric, within each map's non-overlapping 4x4 windows. No cross-frame merges.
shared_design.aggregation: Use pinned ToMe mass-weighted means for memory content and the existing log-mass attention correction. The correction is approximate when key/value vectors differ.
shared_design.temporal_position: Keep native age embeddings 1..6; reuse the oldest native non-conditioning age slot for ages 7..10 in both conditions, then restore native model state on exit.
shared_design.parameters: No training; all pretrained SAM2 parameters remain frozen.

required_checks: Archived native reference provenance and prompt index match the manifest, checkpoint and model config.
Both conditions exactly reproduce archived native predictions and stored outputs until ToMe compression starts (at most six non-conditioning maps).
The full clip reaches at least one target with more than six non-conditioning maps and actually reduces spatial K/V keys there.
All four memory-attention layers are called once per target; every frame/window has the frozen exact quota and cluster provenance.
Spatial token mass is conserved, pointers remain unchanged, K/V input alignment is valid, all outputs are finite, and model parameters are unchanged.
Extended temporal embeddings and num_maskmem are restored after each condition.
Two fresh processes reproduce prediction hashes, stored-output hashes, quota traces and merge provenance exactly for each condition.
The two conditions use the same frame/window quotas. No Dice effect or candidate efficacy conclusion is inferred from this gate.
stop_rule: Any integrity, parity or replay failure blocks efficacy testing. Fix only a demonstrated implementation defect and rerun this gate. Do not tune this candidate on PolypGen; require untouched-data evaluation for efficacy claims.

references.title: Token Merging: Your ViT But Faster
ALGM: Adaptive Local-then-Global Token Merging for Efficient Semantic Segmentation with Plain Vision Transformers
SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
